<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-action-reference.mjs from action.yml of jscpd 5.4.2. Edit the script or action.yml in the jscpd repository, not this file. -->

`kucherenko/jscpd@v5` runs the same binary as the command line, so every input below is a [CLI option](/reference/cli) with the same name. The [CI guide](/guides/ci) shows the workflows; this page is the list.

```yaml [.github/workflows/jscpd.yml]
- uses: kucherenko/jscpd@v5
  with:
    threshold: 3
```

## Inputs

| Input | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | Paths to scan for duplicates (space-separated) | `.` |
| `config` | Path to .jscpd.json config file | — |
| `min-tokens` | Minimum number of tokens to consider a duplicate | `50` |
| `min-lines` | Minimum number of lines to consider a duplicate | `5` |
| `max-lines` | Maximum lines per block to consider | — |
| `mode` | Detection mode: mild, weak, or strict | `mild` |
| `format` | Comma-separated list of file extensions/formats to check | — |
| `ignore` | Comma-separated glob patterns to ignore | — |
| `ignore-pattern` | Comma-separated regex patterns to skip matching tokens | — |
| `reporters` | Comma-separated list of reporters (console, json, xml, csv, html, markdown, badge, sarif, ai, xcode, console-full, threshold, silent) | `console` |
| `output` | Output directory for file reporters | `report` |
| `report-name` | Base name of the report files, without the extension (jscpd --report-name; default jscpd-report). The action reads <report-name>.json and .sarif back, so set it here, not only as reportName in .jscpd.json | — |
| `threshold` | Maximum duplication percentage before exit 1 | — |
| `baseline` | Path to a clone baseline file (e.g. .jscpd-baseline.json): clones absent from it are reported as new | — |
| `update-baseline` | Rewrite the baseline file from the current run (requires baseline) | `false` |
| `fail-on-new-clones` | Exit 1 when new clones are found (requires baseline or baseline-from-ref). Use 'true' for zero tolerance, or an integer N to allow up to N new clones | — |
| `fail-on-empty` | Exit 1 when the scan analyzes no files: the paths exist but nothing matched the format, ignore or pattern filters | `false` |
| `baseline-from-ref` | Compare against an ephemeral baseline built from a git ref's tree (e.g. origin/main); needs the ref fetched (fetch-depth: 0). Conflicts with baseline | — |
| `history` | Duplication and health trend over git history: 'true' for the last 30 commits of the branch (or the config's history range), or a range of commits to scan (e.g. v5.0.0..HEAD); 'false' leaves it off. Prints charts and a table in the log and needs the commits fetched (fetch-depth: 0, or 30 for 'true') | — |
| `blame` | Enrich clones with git blame data | `false` |
| `exit-code` | Exit with code when duplicates found. Use 'true' for default code 1, or an integer like '2' for a custom code | — |
| `pattern` | Glob pattern to find files to scan | — |
| `max-size` | Skip files larger than SIZE (e.g. 100kb, 1mb) | — |
| `skip-local` | Skip clones where both fragments are in the same directory | `false` |
| `ignore-case` | Ignore case of symbols (experimental) | `false` |
| `ignore-identifiers` | Treat identifiers as equal (Type-2 clones: renamed variables, functions, types): 'consistent' lets a name stand for one name on the other side only, 'blind' lets any name match any other, in similarity too, 'true' takes the matching from the config's ignoreIdentifiers, else consistent | `false` |
| `ignore-literals` | Treat all string and numeric literals as equal | `false` |
| `ignore-annotations` | Skip annotations and decorators (@Name, @Name(...)) | `false` |
| `max-gap-lines` | Merge clones separated by at most N unmatched lines into one near-miss clone (Type-3); 0 disables | `0` |
| `similarity` | Report pairs of functions whose normalized syntax trees share at least this ratio of their subtrees (a number in (0, 1], such as 0.8) as near-miss clones. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#, Go, Rust, C, C++, PHP, Ruby, Swift and Clojure; test files are left out. Not set: the config's value, else off | — |
| `min-nodes` | The fewest nodes of a normalized syntax tree a function needs for similarity to compare it. Not set: the config's value, else 20 | — |
| `follow-symlinks` | Follow symbolic links | `false` |
| `no-gitignore` | Do not respect .gitignore files | `false` |
| `absolute` | Use absolute paths in reports | `false` |
| `formats-exts` | Custom format-to-extension mappings (e.g. javascript:es,es6;dart:dt) | — |
| `formats-names` | Custom format-to-filename mappings (e.g. python:Tiltfile,BUCK;ruby:Buildfile) | — |
| `version` | Version of jscpd to install (default: latest) | `latest` |
| `install-prefix` | Installation directory for the cpd binary (default: /usr/local/bin on Linux/macOS, npm global bin on Windows) | — |
| `skip-install` | Skip installation (use when jscpd/cpd is already installed) | `false` |
| `extra-args` | Additional arguments passed directly to cpd/jscpd | — |
| `upload-report` | Upload the report directory as a workflow artifact | `false` |
| `upload-sarif` | Upload SARIF report to GitHub Code Scanning | `true` |

## Outputs

| Output | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `duplication-percentage` | Percentage of duplicated code found |
| `clones-found` | Number of clone pairs found |
| `duplicated-lines` | Number of duplicated lines |
| `total-lines` | Total number of lines scanned |
| `files-count` | Number of source files scanned |
| `report-path` | Path to the output directory |
| `sarif-path` | Path to the SARIF report file (empty if not generated) |
| `exit-code` | Exit code from jscpd (non-zero if threshold exceeded or --exit-code used) |

Read an output in a later step as `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<name> }}` after giving the jscpd step an `id`.
